items.stem: Complete the statement: Net realisable value is …
options: the expected selling price less the costs of completing and selling the item
the cost of the item plus profit
the replacement cost of the item
items.answer: the expected selling price less the costs of completing and selling the item
items.markingKey: the expected selling price less the costs of completing and selling the item. IAS 2 definition [1]

items.stem: Explain why inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
items.answer: Applying prudence: if goods can only be sold for less than they cost, the loss is recognised now; unrealised profits are not recognised until the goods are sold.
items.markingKey: Prudence [1]; losses recognised, gains not [1] [2]

items.stem: State two reasons why the net realisable value of inventory may fall below cost.
items.answer: Goods are damaged or obsolete; fashion has changed; selling prices have fallen; costs to complete/sell have risen.
items.markingKey: Any two [1 each] [2]

items.stem: Explain why FIFO gives a higher profit than AVCO when prices are rising.
items.answer: FIFO charges the older, cheaper costs to cost of sales and leaves newer, dearer goods in closing inventory, so cost of sales is lower and profit higher.
items.markingKey: Older cheaper costs in COS [1]; higher closing inventory → higher profit [1] [2]

items.stem: State one advantage and one disadvantage of AVCO.
items.answer: Advantage: smooths out price fluctuations / acceptable under IAS 2. Disadvantage: average must be recalculated after every receipt; values do not match actual prices paid.
items.markingKey: Advantage [1]; disadvantage [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why an error in closing inventory affects the profit of two years.
items.answer: Closing inventory of one year is the opening inventory of the next; an overstatement raises this year's profit and reduces next year's by the same amount.

items.stem: Explain how an overstatement of closing inventory affects the statement of financial position.

items.answer: The earliest prices were used; under FIFO the earliest units are issued first so closing inventory is at the latest prices. Correct FIFO value: $1,220.00.
